1	# Environment Setup
2	
3	**Goal:** Resolve the project root before any other operations.
4	
5	## Studio Desktop vs headless Studio
6	
7	`uip rpa` runs against a **headless Studio** by default (codename Helm — ships as the `UiPath.Studio.Helm.{Platform}` NuGet package, auto-launched the first time a command needs it). **Studio Desktop is not required** for the standard authoring loop — `init`, `run`, `debug start`, `validate`, `build`, `activities find`, `packages install`, the `uia` group (indication, capture, interaction), etc. all work headless.
8	
9	Studio Desktop is only required for two interactive UI tools:
10	- `uip rpa files diff` — opens an interactive diff window in Studio's UI.
11	- `uip rpa focus-activity` — selects an activity in Studio's active workflow designer.
12	
13	For these two, see [§ Edge case: requiring Studio Desktop](#edge-case-requiring-studio-desktop) below.
14	
15	> **First call is slow.** On a cold NuGet cache, the very first `uip rpa` invocation triggers a silent `dotnet restore` of the headless Studio package and may sit near-silent for 30–90 seconds (longer behind a slow feed). A heartbeat line every 15s confirms it's still working. The default shell timeout covers this; bump `timeoutSeconds` only behind a slow feed.
16	
17	## Step 0.1: Establish Project Root
18	
19	The `uip rpa` commands use `--project-dir` to target a specific project (defaults to current working directory). **If the current working directory is NOT the UiPath project root, all commands will fail or target the wrong project.**
20	
21	**Resolution order** (use the first rule that matches):
22	1. **Explicit path** — The user provided a directory path → use it as-is.
23	2. **Project name reference** — The user mentioned a project by name → search for a folder with that name containing `project.json`.
24	3. **Fall back to current working directory** — If neither is given.
25	
26	If the CWD is not the project root:
27	- Locate the project root by finding `project.json`: `Glob: pattern="**/project.json"`
28	- **Pass `--project-dir` explicitly** to every `uip rpa` command
29	- Store the project root path and use it consistently as `{projectRoot}`
30	
31	## Step 0.2: Authentication (If Needed)
32	
33	Some commands (IS connections, workflow examples, cloud features) require authentication:
34	
35	```bash
36	uip login
37	```
38	
39	If you encounter auth errors (401, 403, "not authenticated") during any phase, prompt the user to run `uip login` to authenticate against their UiPath Cloud tenant.
40	
41	## Step 0.3: Creating a New Project
42	
43	**ALWAYS use `uip rpa init`** — never write `project.json`, `project.uiproj`, or other scaffolding files manually.
44	
45	**`init` always scaffolds XAML.** Regardless of flags, the templates produce XAML files: `BlankTemplate` → `Main.xaml`, `TestAutomationProjectTemplate` → `TestCase.xaml`, `LibraryProcessTemplate` → XAML library workflows. There is no flag that flips the scaffolding to coded.
46	
47	**`--expression-language` is independent of coded vs XAML.** It controls VB vs C# syntax inside XAML activity expressions — not whether the project has `.cs` workflow files. Coded workflows (`.cs` with `[Workflow]` / `[TestCase]`) work fine in both `VisualBasic` and `CSharp` projects.
48	
49	**To work in coded mode**, scaffold the project (always XAML), then add `.cs` workflow files following [coded/operations-guide.md § Add a Workflow File](coded/operations-guide.md#add-a-workflow-file-to-existing-project) and update `entryPoints` in `project.json`. The scaffolded `Main.xaml` / `TestCase.xaml` can stay alongside your `.cs` files — `.xaml` and `.cs` workflows coexist freely.
50	
51	**First, decide which template to use** — see [§ Template selection](#template-selection) below **before** running any `init` command. Defaulting to `--template-id BlankTemplate` is correct only when the user did not name a template or domain pattern.
52	
53	### For XAML Projects (default for new projects)
54	
55	```bash
56	uip rpa init \
57	  --name "MyAutomation" \
58	  --location "/path/to/parent/directory" \
59	  --template-id "BlankTemplate" \
60	  --expression-language <VisualBasic|CSharp> \
61	  --target-framework <Windows|Portable> \
62	  --description "Automates invoice processing" \
63	  --output json
64	```
65	
66	**Decide `--target-framework` and `--expression-language` before running — never omit them.** Both are immutable after creation; omitting `--target-framework` silently produces a **Windows** project. The placeholder shows the two new-project options (`Windows`, `Portable`). Windows - Legacy is a last resort (explicit ask or hard .NET 4.6.1 need) and is created/authored in **Legacy mode**, not via this command. Choose from runtime / host-OS signals per SKILL.md Common Rule 2a.
67	
68	**Expression language:** Default `VisualBasic`. Use `CSharp` only when the user explicitly asks for C# expressions inside XAML activities.
69	
70	**`--studio-dir`:** Optional. Headless Studio does not need it. Pass it only when you have explicitly forced Studio Desktop (`UIPATH_RPA_TOOL_USE_STUDIO=1`, or invoking `diff`/`focus-activity`) and Studio's auto-detection from the registry fails.
71	
72	### For Coded Projects (only when the user explicitly requested coded)
73	
74	Run the **same** `init` command as for an XAML project (above) — there is no separate coded form. After it scaffolds, add `.cs` workflow files per [coded/operations-guide.md § Add a Workflow File](coded/operations-guide.md#add-a-workflow-file-to-existing-project) and update `entryPoints` in `project.json`. The scaffolded `Main.xaml` / `TestCase.xaml` can stay — remove it only if the user explicitly asks for a coded-only project.
75	
76	#### Parameters
77	
78	| Parameter | Options | Default | Notes |
79	|-----------|---------|---------|-------|
80	| `--name` | Any string | (required) | Project folder name |
81	| `--location` | Directory path | (current dir) | Parent directory where project folder is created |
82	| `--template-id` | `BlankTemplate`, `LibraryProcessTemplate`, `TestAutomationProjectTemplate` | `BlankTemplate` | Project template |
83	| `--expression-language` | `VisualBasic`, `CSharp` | none — set explicitly | Expression syntax for XAML workflows. Immutable after creation |
84	| `--target-framework` | `Windows`, `Portable` (Cross-platform), `Legacy` (Windows - Legacy) | none — set explicitly (omitting → Windows) | .NET target framework. Immutable after creation. `Legacy` is a last resort for new projects (explicit ask or hard .NET 4.6.1 need only). Decide per Rule 2a |
85	| `--description` | Any string | (none) | Project description in project.json |
86	
87	**Note:** `uip rpa init` may return `success: false` but still create the project files (partial success). If it fails, check whether the project directory and `project.json` were created before retrying.
88	
89	### Template selection
90	
91	Before running `init`, decide which template to use.
92	
93	**1. Trigger keywords**
94	
95	| User says... | Action |
96	|---|---|
97	| "REFramework", "ERP template", "SAP template", "based on X template", or any specific template name | Run `uip rpa templates search --query "<term>" --output json` (see § "Search and select" below) |
98	| "library", "library project" | Use `--template-id LibraryProcessTemplate` (built-in, no search) |
99	| "test project", "test automation" | Use `--template-id TestAutomationProjectTemplate` (built-in, no search) |
100	| Nothing template-related | Use `--template-id BlankTemplate` (default) |
101	
102	**2. Search and select**
103	
104	Run `uip rpa templates search --query "<term>" --output json`. Apply this rule against `Data[*]`, top-down:
105	
106	- **User named a specific non-Official template** (e.g. "Enhanced REFramework", "Lite ReFrameWork", a specific package name) AND a `Marketplace` item's `title` or `packageId` substring-matches the user's specific qualifier ("Enhanced", "Lite", etc.) → ask the user (treat Official + that Marketplace item as candidates). Do NOT auto-pick.
107	- **Exactly one item with `source == "Official"`** AND user did not name a non-Official template → pick it. No user prompt.
108	- **Multiple `Official` items** → present candidates (`packageId`, `version`, `title`, `description`) and ask the user.
109	- **Zero `Official` items, ≥1 `Marketplace` item** → present and ask. Never silently pick a Marketplace template.
110	- **No results** → tell the user, then create with `--template-id BlankTemplate`.
111	
112	**3. Create from package**
113	
114	For Official/Marketplace templates, pass `--template-package-id` (and optionally `--template-package-version` — omit for latest) to `init`. When `--template-package-id` is set, `--template-id` is ignored.
115	
116	### From a NuGet Template Package
117	
118	Use when the user asks for a domain-specific template, references a specific template package by name, or wants to browse available templates.
119	
120	**1. Search for available templates:**
121	
122	```bash
123	uip rpa templates search --query "<SEARCH_TERM>" --output json
124	```
125	
126	Does not require a project to be open. Returns a JSON array of `TemplateSearchResult` objects:
127	
128	```json
129	[
130	  {
131	    "packageId": "UiPath.Template.SAPExample",
132	    "version": "2.0.0",
133	    "title": "SAP Automation Template",
134	    "description": "Pre-configured project for SAP GUI automation",
135	    "authors": "UiPath",
136	    "source": "https://feed.example.com/v3/index.json",
137	    "tags": ["SAP", "ERP"]
138	  }
139	]
140	```
141	
142	| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
143	|-----------|------|---------|-------|
144	| `--query` | string | (none) | Filter by name or description. Omit to list all |
145	| `--limit` | integer | 20 | Maximum results |
146	| `--include-prerelease` | flag | false | Include prerelease versions |
147	
148	**2. Create from the chosen template:**
149	
150	```bash
151	uip rpa init \
152	  --name "MySAPAutomation" \
153	  --location "/path/to/parent/directory" \
154	  --template-package-id "<PACKAGE_ID>" \
155	  --template-package-version "<VERSION>" \
156	  --target-framework <Windows|Portable> \
157	  --expression-language <VisualBasic|CSharp> \
158	  --output json
159	```
160	
161	Pass `--target-framework` and `--expression-language` here too (Rule 2a) — a template package does not exempt you from the explicit-framework decision.
162	
163	| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
164	|-----------|------|---------|-------|
165	| `--template-package-id` | string | (none) | NuGet package ID from `templates search` results. **Overrides `--template-id` when set** |
166	| `--template-package-version` | string | (latest) | Omit to use the latest available version |
167	
168	### After Creation
169	
170	1. Open the project in Studio: `uip rpa project open --project-dir "/path/to/MyAutomation"`
171	2. **Read the scaffolded files** — the command generates starter files. Read them before making changes so you build on valid defaults
172	3. Proceed with the skill workflow using the new project root
173	
174	> **Batch the post-`init` prerequisites.** Step 2 here, `packages install` for known-needed packages, and the first `activities find` all depend only on the project existing — emit them as parallel tool calls in one message, not one per turn. They share the warmed Studio host. See SKILL.md § Call Batching.
175	
176	## Edge case: requiring Studio Desktop
177	
178	Two `uip rpa` commands need a running Studio Desktop instance — they have UI side effects that Helm cannot render:
179	
180	| Command | Why it needs Studio |
181	|---------|---------------------|
182	| `uip rpa files diff` | Opens an interactive diff window in Studio's UI; finishes when the user closes the window. |
183	| `uip rpa focus-activity` | Selects/highlights an activity in Studio's active workflow designer. ⚠️ Against headless it **silently succeeds without doing anything** (there is no designer) — a `success: true` from a headless session does NOT mean anything was focused. |
184	
185	When (and only when) you need to run one of these, ensure Studio Desktop is up:
186	
187	```bash
188	uip rpa instances list --output json   # hidden diagnostic — confirms a Studio Desktop instance is running
189	uip rpa studio start --project-dir "{projectRoot}" --output json   # launches Studio Desktop if none is running
190	```
191	
192	If `studio start` cannot resolve Studio's install directory from the registry, pass `--studio-dir` pointing to the Studio installation root.
193	
194	You can also force Studio Desktop for any other command by setting `UIPATH_RPA_TOOL_USE_STUDIO=1`, but this is not needed for the standard authoring loop and gives up the headless benefits.

1	# XAML Basics and Rules
2	
3	Core concepts for UiPath workflow XAML files and rules for generating and/or editing XAML content.
4	
5	## XAML File Anatomy
6	
7	Every UiPath XAML workflow file has this structure:
8	
9	**`x:Class` naming rule:** The value must match the file's relative path from the project root (without the `.xaml` extension), with folder separators replaced by **underscores** — not dots. For a root-level file `MyWorkflow.xaml` → `x:Class="MyWorkflow"`. For a file in a subfolder `Workflows/SendEmail.xaml` → `x:Class="Workflows_SendEmail"`. Using dots (e.g., `Workflows.SendEmail`) causes a validation error: *"Invalid ActivityBuilder name … Suggested name …"*.
10	
11	```xml
12	<Activity mc:Ignorable="sap sap2010 sads" x:Class="FolderName_FileName"
13	  xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities"
14	  xmlns:mc="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/markup-compatibility/2006"
15	  xmlns:sap="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities/presentation"
16	  xmlns:sap2010="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2010/xaml/activities/presentation"
17	  xmlns:sads="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2010/xaml/activities/debugger"
18	  xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
19	  <!-- Additional xmlns for activity packages -->
20	  >
21	
22	  <!-- TextExpression.NamespacesForImplementation (C# imports) -->
23	  <TextExpression.NamespacesForImplementation>
24	    <sco:Collection x:TypeArguments="x:String"
25	      xmlns:sco="clr-namespace:System.Collections.ObjectModel;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib">
26	      <x:String>System</x:String>
27	      <x:String>System.Collections.Generic</x:String>
28	      <x:String>System.Linq</x:String>
29	      <!-- More namespace imports -->
30	    </sco:Collection>
31	  </TextExpression.NamespacesForImplementation>
32	
33	  <!-- TextExpression.ReferencesForImplementation (assembly references) -->
34	  <TextExpression.ReferencesForImplementation>
35	    <sco:Collection x:TypeArguments="AssemblyReference"
36	      xmlns:sco="clr-namespace:System.Collections.ObjectModel;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib">
37	      <AssemblyReference>System</AssemblyReference>
38	      <!-- More assembly references -->
39	    </sco:Collection>
40	  </TextExpression.ReferencesForImplementation>
41	
42	  <!-- x:Members (arguments) -->
43	  <x:Members>
44	    <x:Property Name="in_Name" Type="InArgument(x:String)" />
45	    <x:Property Name="out_Result" Type="OutArgument(x:Int32)" />
46	    <x:Property Name="io_Data" Type="InOutArgument(x:String)" />
47	  </x:Members>
48	
49	  <!-- Main workflow body -->
50	  <Sequence DisplayName="Main Sequence">
51	    <Sequence.Variables>
52	      <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:String" Name="tempVar" Default="hello" />
53	    </Sequence.Variables>
54	    <!-- Activities go here -->
55	  </Sequence>
56	
57	  <!-- ViewState (designer metadata - DO NOT EDIT) -->
58	  <sap2010:WorkflowViewState.ViewStateManager>
59	    <!-- ... -->
60	  </sap2010:WorkflowViewState.ViewStateManager>
61	</Activity>
62	```
63	
64	## Workflow Types
65	
66	### Sequence
67	Linear, step-by-step execution. Best for straightforward processes.
68	```xml
69	<Sequence DisplayName="My Sequence">
70	  <!-- Activities execute top to bottom -->
71	</Sequence>
72	```
73	
74	### Flowchart
75	Branching logic with decision nodes. Best for complex decision flows.
76	
77	**Key pattern:** All FlowStep/FlowDecision/FlowSwitch nodes are direct children of `<Flowchart>`; wire them via `<x:Reference>` inside property elements (`Flowchart.StartNode`, `FlowStep.Next`, `FlowDecision.True/False`). NEVER nest one `FlowStep` inside another's `<FlowStep.Next>` — nested-only steps are absent from `Flowchart.Nodes` and won't render.
78	
79	```xml
80	<Flowchart DisplayName="My Flowchart" sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="Flowchart_1">
81	  <Flowchart.StartNode>
82	    <x:Reference>__ReferenceID0</x:Reference>
83	  </Flowchart.StartNode>
84	  <FlowStep x:Name="__ReferenceID0">
85	    <!-- Activity here -->
86	    <FlowStep.Next>
87	      <x:Reference>__ReferenceID1</x:Reference>
88	    </FlowStep.Next>
89	  </FlowStep>
90	  <FlowDecision x:Name="__ReferenceID1">
91	    <FlowDecision.Condition>
92	      <CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean">condition</CSharpValue>
93	    </FlowDecision.Condition>
94	    <FlowDecision.True>
95	      <x:Reference>__ReferenceID0</x:Reference>
96	    </FlowDecision.True>
97	    <!-- FlowDecision.False omitted = end of flow -->
98	  </FlowDecision>
99	</Flowchart>
100	```
101	
102	Node vocabulary, structure & wiring rules, the forbidden nested-chain pattern, node registration, condition expressions (VB/C#), and layout: [flowchart-guide.md](flowchart-guide.md). Layout coordinates and ViewState recipes: [canvas-layout-guide.md § Flowchart Layout](canvas-layout-guide.md#3-flowchart-layout).
103	
104	### State Machine
105	State-based workflow with transitions. Best for long-running processes with distinct states (e.g., REFramework).
106	
107	```xml
108	<StateMachine InitialState="{x:Reference __ReferenceID0}" DisplayName="My State Machine"
109	              sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="StateMachine_1">
110	  <State x:Name="__ReferenceID0" DisplayName="Initial State">
111	    <State.Entry>
112	      <Sequence DisplayName="Initialize">
113	        <!-- Activities when entering state -->
114	      </Sequence>
115	    </State.Entry>
116	    <State.Transitions>
117	      <Transition DisplayName="To Processing">
118	        <Transition.Condition>[condition]</Transition.Condition>
119	        <Transition.To>
120	          <x:Reference>__ReferenceID1</x:Reference>
121	        </Transition.To>
122	      </Transition>
123	    </State.Transitions>
124	  </State>
125	  <State x:Name="__ReferenceID1" DisplayName="Processing">
126	    <!-- State.Entry, State.Transitions -->
127	  </State>
128	  <State x:Name="__ReferenceID2" DisplayName="End" IsFinal="True" />
129	</StateMachine>
130	```
131	
132	**Key patterns:**
133	- `InitialState` attribute references the starting State
134	- States are direct children of `<StateMachine>` (no wrapper element)
135	- `IsFinal="True"` marks the terminal state
136	- Transitions use `<Transition.To><x:Reference>__ReferenceID</x:Reference></Transition.To>` child element pattern
137	
138	**ViewState is needed** for usable State Machine layout. See [canvas-layout-guide.md § State Machine Layout](canvas-layout-guide.md#4-state-machine-layout) for coordinate systems, transition connection points, and recipes.
139	
140	### Long Running Workflow (ProcessDiagram)
141	BPMN-style horizontal flow for event-driven, long-running processes. Uses `upa:ProcessDiagram` with `EventNode`, `TaskNode`, `DecisionNode`, and `EndNode`.
142	
143	Requires additional namespaces:
144	```xml
145	xmlns:upa="clr-namespace:UiPath.Process.Activities;assembly=UiPath.Process.Activities"
146	xmlns:upas="clr-namespace:UiPath.Process.Activities.Shared;assembly=UiPath.Process.Activities"
147	```
148	
149	These types ship in the **`UiPath.FlowchartBuilder.Activities`** package (runtime assembly `UiPath.Process.Activities`) — install before authoring (Common Rule 6). Not supported on `targetFramework: "Legacy"`. Package install, full node vocabulary, gateway patterns, suspend/resume: [long-running-workflow-guide.md](long-running-workflow-guide.md).
150	
151	```xml
152	<upa:ProcessDiagram DisplayName="Long Running Workflow" sap2010:WorkflowViewState.IdRef="ProcessDiagram_1">
153	  <upa:ProcessDiagram.StartNode>
154	    <x:Reference>__ReferenceID0</x:Reference>
155	  </upa:ProcessDiagram.StartNode>
156	  <upa:EventNode x:Name="__ReferenceID0" DisplayName="Manual Trigger">
157	    <upa:EventNode.Behavior>
158	      <upa:StartBehavior>
159	        <upa:StartBehavior.DesignerMetadata>
160	          <upas:DesignerMetadata NodeType="StartEvent.Interrupting.None" />
161	        </upa:StartBehavior.DesignerMetadata>
162	      </upa:StartBehavior>
163	    </upa:EventNode.Behavior>
164	    <upa:EventNode.Next>
165	      <upa:TaskNode x:Name="__ReferenceID1" DisplayName="Process">
166	        <upa:TaskNode.Behavior>
167	          <upa:NodeBehavior>
168	            <upa:NodeBehavior.DesignerMetadata>
169	              <upas:DesignerMetadata NodeType="Task.None" />
170	            </upa:NodeBehavior.DesignerMetadata>
171	          </upa:NodeBehavior>
172	        </upa:TaskNode.Behavior>
173	        <Sequence DisplayName="Process Steps">
174	          <!-- Activities here -->
175	        </Sequence>
176	      </upa:TaskNode>
177	    </upa:EventNode.Next>
178	  </upa:EventNode>
179	  <!-- Register inline nodes -->
180	  <x:Reference>__ReferenceID1</x:Reference>
181	</upa:ProcessDiagram>
182	```
183	
184	**Key patterns:**
185	- Flows **left-to-right** (horizontal), not top-to-bottom
186	- `EventNode` = start/end circles, `TaskNode` = activity rectangles, `DecisionNode` = diamond (True/False branches), `EndNode` = end circle
187	- `BoundaryNode` attaches to `TaskNode.BoundaryNodes` for error handling
188	- Same `<x:Reference>` node registration rules as Flowchart — inline nodes need trailing registration
189	- Gateway nodes (`SplitNode`/`MergeNode`/`SwitchNode<T>`), subprocesses, intermediate events, and persistence-based waits: [long-running-workflow-guide.md](long-running-workflow-guide.md)
190	
191	**ViewState is needed.** See [canvas-layout-guide.md § Long Running Workflow](canvas-layout-guide.md#5-long-running-workflow-processdiagram-layout) for horizontal layout recipes.
192	
193	## XAML Safety Rules
194	
195	Critical rules to follow when editing XAML files to prevent validation errors and workflow corruption.
196	
197	### ViewState Rules
198	
199	ViewState controls how activities appear in the visual designer. Rules differ by workflow type and operation:
200	
201	**Sequences:** ViewState is optional — Studio auto-manages `IsExpanded` state. No coordinates needed.
202	
203	**Flowcharts, State Machines, Long Running Workflows:** ViewState is **mandatory** — it determines node positions on the 2D canvas. Without it, Studio stacks every node at (0,0): they overlap into what looks like **a single node**. Studio does **not** auto-arrange on open — the stacked layout persists until a user manually triggers Auto Arrange. Always generate ViewState for these workflow types.
204	
205	**When editing existing files:**
206	- Do NOT modify the global `<sap2010:WorkflowViewState.ViewStateManager>` section — it can corrupt the designer layout
207	- Do NOT modify existing ViewState on nodes you are not changing
208	- When adding new nodes to a Flowchart/StateMachine, read existing node positions first to avoid overlap
209	
210	**When generating new Flowchart/StateMachine/ProcessDiagram files:**
211	- Generate ViewState for every node to produce a usable layout: `ShapeLocation` + `ShapeSize` are required; `ConnectorLocation` is optional (Studio auto-routes connectors from node positions)
212	- See [canvas-layout-guide.md](canvas-layout-guide.md) for coordinate systems, standard sizes, and layout recipes
213	
214	> **Why the distinction?** Sequences stack children vertically on their own, so coordinates are unnecessary. Flowcharts, State Machines, and ProcessDiagrams are 2D canvases with no implicit ordering — Studio cannot place nodes it has no coordinates for, so it leaves them all at (0,0). The result reads as one overlapping node. Generate ViewState for every node so the workflow renders as separate, connected nodes.

226	### Activity Property Surface and Starter XAML
227	
228	Never construct activity XAML from memory. Two sources, in this order:
229	
230	1. **`<Activity>.md`** — authoritative property surface: which properties exist, types, defaults, descriptions, required-scope rules.
231	2. **`uip rpa activities get-default-xaml --activity-class-name "<FullClassName>"`** — starter element with correct namespaces, assembly references, and any properties whose values differ from the type default.
232	
233	**Where `<Activity>.md` lives — try in this order:**
234	
235	1. **Primary:** `{PROJECT_DIR}/.local/docs/packages/<PackageId>/activities/<Activity>.md` — auto-generated when the package is installed; co-versioned with the runtime. Use `Glob` + `Read` (not `Grep` — `.local/` is gitignored).
236	2. **Fallback:** `skills/uipath-rpa/references/activity-docs/<PackageId>/<closest-version>/<Activity>.md` — bundled reference set covering the major UiPath packages. Use this when `.local/docs` is empty for that package (older versions don't ship per-activity docs) or when no project directory is in scope yet. Pick the version folder closest to the installed version.
237	3. **Neither exists:** the package is third-party or unusual. Document this in your output, fall back to `activities find` + `activities get-default-xaml` alone, and warn the user that the property surface may be incomplete.
238	
239	> **Skip-tax.** `activities get-default-xaml` omits any property whose value equals the type default (`null`, `0`, `false`, unset). For `NTypeInto`: 2 of 20 properties. For `NClick`: ~3 of ~15. For `NGetText`: every output property — the starter is literally `<uix:NGetText HealingAgentBehavior="SameAsCard" />`, with no output member visible. Authoring from this starter alone is how `NGetText.Value="..."` gets written — `Value` does not exist on that activity, so `validate` accepts it as static-clean and `build` finally rejects it as an unknown member. The starter looks complete; it isn't. The MD read is the only way you learn which properties actually exist (`TextString`, `ClickType`, `KeyModifiers`, `WaitForReady`, `EmptyFieldMode`, etc.). **When authoring a new Get Text, bind the output to `TextString`** (`OutArgument<string>`) — the typed member the current designer surfaces. But `NGetText` declares **two** real output members: `TextString` and a legacy non-generic `Text` `OutArgument` (backwards-compat — the activity writes the scraped text to both at runtime, and the designer hides whichever the installed version does not use). So a `Text="..."` binding in an existing or older workflow is valid and must not be flagged or "corrected" — only `Value` is a genuine unknown member.
240	
241	**Workflow — each step depends on the previous step's output:**
242	
243	1. `uip rpa activities find --query "<keyword>" --output json` → fully qualified class name, type ID, `isDynamicActivity` flag.
244	2. **Locate `<Activity>.md` (primary → fallback per the lookup order above) and write an explicit property checklist** — required properties for the activity to function, plus optional properties relevant to your use case. If neither doc location has the file, record that explicitly and proceed to step 3 with a flag in your output. If you cannot name at least the required properties from the doc you found, you read the wrong file.
245	3. `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` → starter element with namespaces and assembly references.
246	4. **Diff your step-2 checklist against the step-3 starter.** Add every checklist property that isn't already in the starter. An empty checklist with no third-party flag from step 2 means step 2 was skipped — go back to step 2; do NOT author from the starter alone.
247	5. Validate with `uip rpa validate`.
248	
249	**The rule binds for every activity not on the [common-activity card](../common-activity-card.md).** Check the card first. If the activity is listed there, author from the card entry and skip `activities find`, `activities get-default-xaml`, and the per-activity doc read. If the activity is not listed there, follow the full workflow above. Self-extending the card by personal judgment ("this one feels simple — `StartProcess`, `InvokeWorkflowFile`, I can skip the procedure") is the bug. For card activities the surface is authoritative — version-anchored, source-verified, curated centrally. For everything else, the procedure is the only check.
250	
251	**Anti-pattern.** Treating `activities get-default-xaml` output as the complete property surface. The CLI runs XAML serialization on a default-constructed instance; type-default values are omitted by design.
252	
253	**Property-name drift.** When `validate` reports `Cannot set unknown member '<Class>.<Prop>'`, the property name is wrong for the installed package version. Check `<Activity>.md` — property names drift between package versions (e.g. UIA `26.4.1-preview` renamed `InputMode` → `InteractionMode`, `EmptyField` → `EmptyFieldMode`).
254	
255	Use `uip rpa workflow-examples list` and `uip rpa workflow-examples get` for usage examples, in addition to searching existing local `.xaml` files.

257	### Container Activity Bodies — Wrap in Sequence
258	
259	Container activities have body or branch slots typed `Activity` or `ActivityAction<T>`. Studio's designer expects each slot to hold a `<Sequence>` drop zone; Studio's serializer emits the wrapped form. **Wrap even single-activity bodies.**
260	
261	| Activity | Slot(s) | Wrapper |
262	|----------|---------|---------|
263	| `If` | `If.Then`, `If.Else` | `<Sequence DisplayName="Then">` / `<Sequence DisplayName="Else">` |
264	| `While`, `DoWhile` | direct child of the activity | `<Sequence DisplayName="Body">` |
265	| `ForEach<T>` | `ForEach.Body` → `ActivityAction<T>` body | `<Sequence DisplayName="Body">` |
266	| `TryCatch` | `TryCatch.Try` | `<Sequence DisplayName="Try">` |
267	| `TryCatch` | each `Catch` → `ActivityAction<T>` body | `<Sequence DisplayName="Catch">` |
268	| `TryCatch` | `TryCatch.Finally` | `<Sequence DisplayName="Finally">` |
269	| `Switch<T>` | `Switch.Default`, each `<x:String x:Key="...">` case | `<Sequence>` per case |
270	| `Pick` | each `PickBranch.Trigger`, `PickBranch.Action` | `<Sequence>` per slot |
271	| `NApplicationCard` | `Body` → `ActivityAction<...>` body | `<Sequence DisplayName="Do">` |
272	| Any activity with `Body` typed `Activity` | the body slot | `<Sequence>` |
273	
274	**Validators do not catch this.** `validate` and `build` both accept any single `Activity` in a body slot — `<If.Then><Throw /></If.Then>` is structurally legal. The wrap is a Studio-idiomatic convention (drop-zone ergonomics + canonical emission), not a static-analysis requirement.
275	
276	**Cheapest enforcement.** For card-listed containers (`If`, `Switch<T>`, `TryCatch`, `While`, `DoWhile`, `ForEach<T>`), copy the wrapped shape from the common-activity card. For off-card containers (`Pick`, `Parallel`, `ParallelForEach<T>`, package-specific body activities), run `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml --activity-class-name "<FullClassName>"` after the Rule 21 doc read and copy the wrapped shape from the starter. See SKILL.md Rules 21, 21a, 24.
277	
278	**Worked example.** [§ Example 1: Basic Activities (LogMessage, If/Else, Assign)](#example-1-basic-activities-logmessage-ifelse-assign) below — `If.Then` and `If.Else` each carry a `<Sequence>`.
279	
280	**Editing existing files.** When inserting an activity into an empty or bare `If.Then` / `Catch` / `Body` slot, add the `<Sequence>` wrapper in the same edit.

295	### Adding Arguments (In/Out/InOut)
296	
297	Add `x:Property` elements inside the `<x:Members>` block:
298	
299	```xml
300	<x:Members>
301	  <!-- In argument (input to workflow) -->
302	  <x:Property Name="in_CustomerName" Type="InArgument(x:String)" />
303	  <!-- Out argument (output from workflow) -->
304	  <x:Property Name="out_ProcessedCount" Type="OutArgument(x:Int32)" />
305	  <!-- InOut argument (both input and output) -->
306	  <x:Property Name="io_DataTable" Type="InOutArgument(scg:List(x:String))" />
307	</x:Members>
308	```
309	
310	Argument naming convention: `in_`, `out_`, `io_` prefixes.
311	
312	#### Setting Default Values for Arguments
313	
314	Defaults go on the root `<Activity>` element using the canonical .NET Workflow Foundation self-namespace syntax:
315	
316	```xml
317	<Activity x:Class="TestCase"
318	          xmlns:this="clr-namespace:"
319	          this:TestCase.in_FileName="report.pdf"
320	          xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities"
321	          xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml">
322	  <x:Members>
323	    <x:Property Name="in_FileName" Type="InArgument(x:String)" />
324	  </x:Members>
325	</Activity>
326	```
327	
328	Two parts are mandatory:
329	
330	1. **`xmlns:this="clr-namespace:"`** — the empty `clr-namespace:` is what makes `this:` resolve to the class declared by `x:Class`.
331	2. **`this:<ClassName>.<argName>="<value>"`** — the attribute name MUST be qualified with `this:` AND the class name; bare `<argName>="<value>"` is rejected.
332	
333	The default is baked into the compiled assembly at build time as a `Literal<T>` expression in the generated class's constructor. At runtime, when the workflow is invoked without that argument supplied (e.g. `uip rpa run` without `--input-arguments`), the literal is used.
334	
335	**Three default-value forms that DO NOT work** — every one of them is rejected by the XAML loader. Authoring agents have repeatedly tried these and lost time to confusing errors — don't:
336	
337	| Bad form | Error |
338	|---|---|
339	| `<Activity in_FileName="...">` (no `xmlns:this`, no class qualifier) | `member (in_FileName) is not supported by DynamicActivity` |
340	| `<x:Property Name="in_FileName" ...><InArgument>...</InArgument></x:Property>` | `DynamicActivityProperty does not have a content property` |
341	| `<x:Property.Value>...</x:Property.Value>` | `x:Property member (Value) is not supported by DynamicActivityProperty` |
342	
343	If you must accept an empty string as a sentinel ("user didn't provide one") and substitute a literal anyway, use a ternary inside each `CSharpValue`/`VisualBasicValue` consumer of the argument:
344	
345	```xml
346	<CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="x:String">string.IsNullOrEmpty(in_FileName) ? "report.pdf" : in_FileName</CSharpValue>
347	```
348	
349	But the root-attribute default above is the cleaner answer — use it first.

351	### Adding Variables
352	
353	Add `Variable` elements inside the workflow container's `.Variables` block:
354	
355	```xml
356	<Sequence.Variables>
357	  <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:String" Name="filePath" />
358	  <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" Name="counter" Default="0" />
359	  <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" Name="isValid" Default="True" />
360	</Sequence.Variables>
361	```
362	
363	Variables are scoped to their containing activity (Sequence, Flowchart, etc.).
364	
365	**IMPORTANT — `x:` and `s:` are XML namespace aliases, not separate type systems.**
366	`x:String` and `s:String` both refer to `System.String`; the prefix only determines which namespace schema resolves the name. The `x:` XAML language schema registers a small fixed set of types (`x:String`, `x:Int32`, `x:Int64`, `x:Double`, `x:Boolean`, `x:Byte`, `x:Single`, `x:Decimal`, `x:Char`, `x:Object`, `x:TimeSpan`). Any other CLR type — including `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `Guid`, etc. — is not registered in that schema and must be reached through `s:` (`xmlns:s="clr-namespace:System;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib"`).
367	Using `x:DateTime` or `x:DateTimeOffset` produces `Cannot create unknown type` at load time.
368	See `common-pitfalls.md` → *"Invalid Use of `x:` Prefix for Non-Builtin CLR Types"* for the full list and examples.

389	### Expressions
390	
391	#### C# Expressions (`expressionLanguage: CSharp`)
392	
393	Applies to XAML workflow files in projects whose `project.json` has `expressionLanguage: CSharp`. These rules govern expressions inside XAML — they are unrelated to coded workflows (`.cs` files), which are plain C# and do not use `CSharpValue` / `CSharpReference` elements.
394	
395	Expressions use explicit `<CSharpValue>` (for read/evaluate) or `<CSharpReference>` (for write/lvalue) elements inside `<InArgument>` / `<OutArgument>`:
396	```xml
397	<Assign DisplayName="Set Name">
398	  <Assign.To>
399	    <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
400	      <CSharpReference x:TypeArguments="x:String">fullName</CSharpReference>
401	    </OutArgument>
402	  </Assign.To>
403	  <Assign.Value>
404	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">
405	      <CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="x:String">firstName + " " + lastName</CSharpValue>
406	    </InArgument>
407	  </Assign.Value>
408	</Assign>
409	```
410	
411	**Important**: Do NOT use `[bracket]` shorthand for expressions. Brackets create `VisualBasicValue` nodes at deserialization time, causing validation failures for C#-only syntax (`null`, `?.`, `??`, `typeof()`, etc.).
412	
413	**Stronger rule for attribute-form bindings on `InArgument<T>` / `OutArgument<T>`:** in XAML projects with `expressionLanguage: CSharp`, any **non-literal** attribute value (`Message="variableName"`, `Text=""Hello " + name"`) is also deserialized as a `VisualBasicValue<T>` and fails at runtime with `JIT compilation is disabled for non-Legacy projects`. The attribute parser defaults to VB regardless of the project's expression language. Use `<CSharpValue>` / `<CSharpReference>` child elements for anything that isn't a plain literal. See [csharp-expression-pitfalls.md](csharp-expression-pitfalls.md) and [csharp-activity-binding-guide.md](csharp-activity-binding-guide.md).
414	
415	**Safe attribute-form values** (no expression evaluator involved, type converter handles them directly):
416	- Literal strings on `InArgument<String>`: `Text="Book trip"`, `DisplayName="Open file"`
417	- Enums: `Level="Info"`, `ClickType="Single"`, `MouseButton="Left"`
418	- Numbers, booleans, `{x:Null}`
419	- `TimeSpan` literals: `Duration="00:00:02"`
420	
421	**For activity-specific recipes** (`LogMessage.Message` as `InArgument<Object>`, `NGetText.TextString` as `OutArgument<String>`, `StartProcess.FileName` with composed paths, `Assign`, `If.Condition`, etc.), see [csharp-activity-binding-guide.md](csharp-activity-binding-guide.md). That file is the canonical lookup for the binding form per common activity property.
422	
423	#### VB Expressions (`expressionLanguage: VisualBasic`)
424	Expressions use VB syntax with `[bracket]` shorthand (VB is the default deserialization target for brackets):
425	```xml
426	<InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">[firstName & " " & lastName]</InArgument>
427	```
428	
429	**Check `project.json` `expressionLanguage` field to determine which syntax to use.**

431	### Resource Types (IResource / ILocalResource)
432	
433	Some activity properties accept `IResource` or `ILocalResource` types instead of plain strings for file inputs. These are part of UiPath's resource abstraction model:
434	
435	| Type | Description | When Used |
436	|------|-------------|-----------|
437	| `IResource` | Generic resource (local file, remote file, cloud attachment) | Activities that accept any file source |
438	| `ILocalResource` | Local file on disk (has `LocalPath` property) | Activities that need a file on the local filesystem |
439	| `IRemoteResource` | Remote resource with a URI and a local copy | Cloud/API-sourced files |
440	
441	**In XAML**, resource-typed properties are typically set via expressions that create the resource:
442	```xml
443	<!-- LocalResource from a file path (C# expression) -->
444	<InArgument x:TypeArguments="upr:ILocalResource">
445	  <CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="upr:ILocalResource">LocalResource.FromPath(filePath)</CSharpValue>
446	</InArgument>
447	```
448	
449	Required namespace for resource types:
450	```xml
451	<x:String>UiPath.Platform.ResourceHandling</x:String>
452	```
453	
454	**Activity Storage**: Some activities use a bucket-based storage system (`.storage/` folder in the project). Resources stored at design-time in `.storage/.runtime/<bucket>/` are packed into the published NuPkg and available at runtime. This is managed automatically — you don't need to edit storage resources directly in XAML.

720	## Property Binding: Attributes vs Child Elements
721	
722	XAML properties can be set in two ways: as XML attributes or as child elements. Both are valid XAML, but some properties only work reliably in one form.
723	
724	### Attribute Syntax (Inline)
725	```xml
726	<ui:LogMessage Message="[myVar]" Level="Info" />
727	```
728	
729	### Child Element Syntax (Property Element)
730	```xml
731	<ui:SomeActivity>
732	  <ui:SomeActivity.Result>
733	    <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String">[outputVar]</OutArgument>
734	  </ui:SomeActivity.Result>
735	</ui:SomeActivity>
736	```
737	
738	### When to Use Which
739	
740	**Simple values** (strings, enums, booleans, VB expressions in brackets) almost always work as attributes:
741	```xml
742	DisplayName="My Activity" Message="[variable]" Level="Info"
743	```
744	
745	**Output properties** (`OutArgument`, `Result`) may require child element syntax. Some activities accept `Result="[var]"` as an attribute; others only work with the expanded child element form. If an attribute-form output binding causes a validation error, try the child element form.
746	
747	**Complex objects** (BackupSlot, MailboxArgument, ActivityAction, dictionaries) always require child element syntax — they cannot be expressed as a single attribute value.
748	
749	**Strings containing literal `[` or `]`** (e.g., UIA special-key tokens like `[k(enter)]`, `[d(ctrl)]`, `[u(ctrl)]`) require child element syntax. The attribute form `Foo="["…[k(enter)]"]"` runs correctly because the runtime VB compiler reads quoted string literals correctly, but the literal brackets inside the string collide with the outer `[ … ]` VB expression markers and the value will not render in Studio. See [common-pitfalls.md § NTypeInto `Text` with literal `[k(...)]` special-key tokens](common-pitfalls.md#ntypeinto-text-with-literal-k-special-key-tokens).
750	
751	### Version-Sensitive Properties
752	
753	Properties may exist in one package version but not another. If `validate` reports "Could not find member 'PropertyName'":
754	1. The property may not exist in the installed package version — remove it
755	2. The property may have been renamed between versions — check examples from the same package version
756	3. Use `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` output as the authoritative set of properties for the installed version
757	
758	## ConnectorActivity Internals
759	
760	Understanding the structure of `isactr:ConnectorActivity` so you know what you can and cannot edit.
761	
762	### Properties (What They Are)
763	
764	| Property | Editable? | Description |
765	|----------|-----------|-------------|
766	| `Configuration` | **NEVER** | ZIP-compressed, Base64-encoded JSON blob containing the full activity schema (fields, types, connector metadata). This is obtained and computed for you using the `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` command. Do not parse, modify, or construct manually. |
767	| `ConnectionId` | Yes (replace GUID) | Integration Service connection GUID. Use `uip is connections list [connector-key]` to discover available connections and their IDs. |
768	| `UiPathActivityTypeId` | **NEVER** | Identifies the specific connector operation. Obtain using `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` or `uip rpa activities find`. |
769	| `DisplayName` | Yes | Human-readable activity name for the designer. |
770	
771	### FieldObjects (Input/Output Interface)
772	
773	`FieldObjects` is the collection of input and output fields. Each `isactr:FieldObject` has:
774	
775	| Attribute | Description |
776	|-----------|-------------|
777	| `Name` | Field identifier (maps to the connector API parameter). Must match exactly what `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` returns. |
778	| `Type` | One of: `FieldArgument` (contains an Activity Argument), `FieldLiteral` (contains a literal value), `FilterTreeValue` (filter builder criteria), `None` (empty). |
779	
780	**What you CAN edit in FieldObjects:**
781	- **Input field values**: Change the `InArgument` value inside a `FieldObject.Value` to set different input data (e.g., change a search query string).
782	- **Bind to variables**: Replace a literal value with a variable reference using `<CSharpValue>` (e.g., `<CSharpValue x:TypeArguments="x:String">myVariable</CSharpValue>`).
783	
784	**What you CANNOT edit:**
785	- Field `Name` values — these must match the connector API schema exactly.
786	- Field `Type` values — these are determined by the connector metadata.
787	- Output field structure — the `OutArgument` types reference JIT-generated assemblies.
788	- Adding/removing FieldObjects — the set of fields comes from `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml`.
789	
790	### JIT-Generated Assemblies
791	
792	Output fields often use types from JIT-compiled assemblies with hashed names:
793	```
794	CDF573A04A6_search_r.VeKd1XI2qK1X56UO2Br3Ui3
795	^connection(last10)   ^operation   ^content hash
796	```
797	
798	These assembly names are:
799	- **Unpredictable** — derived from SHA-512 hashes of the type schema
800	- **Connection-specific** — different connections produce different hashes
801	- **Generated by the runtime** — you cannot create or reference them without `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml`
802	
803	The corresponding namespace imports and assembly references MUST come from `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` output. Never construct them.
804	
805	### What `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` Returns for Dynamic Activities
806	
807	When you call `uip rpa activities get-default-xaml` with `isDynamicActivity: true`, it returns everything needed:
808	1. The complete `<isactr:ConnectorActivity>` XAML element with `Configuration` blob, `UiPathActivityTypeId`, and `FieldObjects`
809	2. All required `xmlns` declarations for the root `<Activity>` element
810	3. All required namespace imports and references
811	
812	Use this output as-is. The only things you should modify are:
813	- `DisplayName` — set a meaningful name
814	- `ConnectionId` — if swapping to a different connection of the same connector type
815	- Input `FieldObject` values — to set the actual data for your workflow

1	# XAML Workflow Guide
2	
3	Discovery-first approach with iterative error-driven refinement for generating and editing XAML workflows. Always understand before acting, start simple, and validate continuously.
4	
5	## Core Principles
6	
7	1. **Activity Docs Are the Source of Truth** — Installed packages may ship structured documentation at `{projectRoot}/.local/docs/packages/{PackageId}/`. When present, these docs contain source-accurate properties, types, defaults, enum values, conditional property groups, and working XAML examples. Always check for them first.
8	2. **Know Before You Write** — **NEVER** generate XAML blind. Understand the project structure, packages, expression language, and existing patterns.
9	3. **Use What You Know, Skip What You Don't Need** — If you already know the package ID and activity class name, go directly to its doc file. Be efficient: the discovery steps are a priority ladder, not a mandatory checklist.
10	4. **Start Minimal, Iterate to Correct** — Start one workflow at a time and break out logic into multiple files if needed. Build one activity at a time within each workflow. Write the smallest working XAML, validate with `uip rpa validate`, fix what breaks, repeat.
11	5. **Validate After Every Change** — **MUST** validate with **both** `validate` and `uip rpa build` after every change. **NEVER** assume an edit succeeded. `validate` clean alone is not validated — it does not catch unknown member names or invalid enum values; `build` does.
12	6. **Fix Errors by Category** — Triage in order: Package → Structure → Type → Activity Properties → Logic.

21	| **EDIT** | "update", "change", "fix", "modify", "add to" | Discovery → Edit |

27	## Phase 1: Discovery
28	
29	**Goal:** Understand project context, leverage installed activity documentation, study existing patterns, identify reusable components, and discover activities before writing any XAML.

31	> **Batch discovery across activities.** When the workflow needs several activities, do NOT run the find → read-doc → `get-default-xaml` triple one activity at a time. Emit all `activities find` calls in parallel, then all `<Activity>.md` `Read`s in parallel, then all `get-default-xaml` calls in parallel (SKILL.md § Call Batching). Only the per-activity *authoring + validate* loop (Phase 2 / Phase 3) stays sequential — discovery fans out.

33	### Step 1.1: Project Structure
34

37	Read: file_path="{projectRoot}/project.json"          → read the project definition

48	### Step 1.2: Discover Activity Documentation (Primary Source)
49	
50	**This is the most important discovery step. Read `<Activity>.md` BEFORE `activities get-default-xaml`, every time, even for activities that look simple.** Installed activity packages ship structured markdown at `{projectRoot}/.local/docs/packages/{PackageId}/activities/<Activity>.md`. The doc is the property surface; the CLI starter is not. `activities get-default-xaml` strips every property at its type default — for `NGetText` that means **all** output properties are absent from the starter, and authoring from the starter produces `NGetText.Value="..."` instead of the real output member `NGetText.TextString`. `validate` does not catch the wrong member name; only `build` does, after a wasted round-trip.
51	
52	**Availability:** Docs exist only for **installed packages** and typically only for **newer package versions**. When the package is not installed, install it first. When docs are missing, update to the latest version, or fall back to `skills/uipath-rpa/references/activity-docs/<PackageId>/<closest-version>/`.

54	#### Filesystem Structure

56	```

75	| **Don't know package** | `Glob` with `**/*.md` in `{projectRoot}/.local/docs/packages/`. `.local/` is gitignored — use `Glob` + `Read`, not `Grep` |

190	
191	```
192	Read: file_path="{projectRoot}/WorkflowToEdit.xaml"
193	Edit: file_path=... old_string=<exact text> new_string=<modified text>
194	```
195	
196	**Critical:** `old_string` must match exactly and be unique. Include surrounding context if needed.
197	
198	---
199	
200	## Phase 3: Validate & Fix Loop
201	
202	**MUST** repeat until 0-error state from **both** `validate` and `build`, or max 5 fix attempts. After 5 attempts, stop and present remaining errors to the user.
203	
204	### Step 3.1: Check for Errors
205	
206	Run both validators per iteration. `validate` catches structural / reference / analyzer issues; `build` catches member-name and enum-value mistakes that `validate` misses (e.g. `NGetText.Value` when the property is `TextString`, `Operator="StartsWith"` when the enum has no such member). See [../validation-guide.md § Validation Iteration Loop](../validation-guide.md#validation-iteration-loop) for the canonical loop.
207	
208	```bash
209	uip rpa validate --file-path "Workflows/MyWorkflow.xaml" --output json
210	uip rpa build "<PROJECT_DIR>" --log-level Warn --output json
211	```
212	
213	`--file-path` must be **relative to the project directory**. Use `--skip-validation` only for quick cached-error checks. Treat `validate` clean as half-done — `build` clean is the signal to exit the loop.
214	
215	### Step 3.2: Categorize and Fix
216	
217	**Fix order:** Package → Structure → Type → Activity Properties → Logic.
218	
219	1. **Package Errors** — Install/update the package. After install, activity docs become available.
220	2. **Structural Errors** — Fix XML structure. Cross-check against [xaml-basics-and-rules.md](xaml-basics-and-rules.md).
221	3. **Type Errors** — Check activity doc for correct types and enum values. For JIT types: [jit-custom-types-schema.md](jit-custom-types-schema.md).
222	4. **Activity Properties Errors** — Read activity doc for properties, conditional groups, valid configurations. Fallback: `activities get-default-xaml`. Watch for OverloadGroup conflicts.
223	5. **Logic Errors** — Verify expression syntax matches project language. For UI automation: use `debug start`; [ui-automation-guide.md](../ui-automation-guide.md) MUST be read IN FULL first (see § Running UI Automation Workflows for the debug procedure).
224	
225	**When stuck:** Defer to user for minor config details. If failing to resolve an activity, consider InvokeCode as a last resort.
226	
227	For detailed procedures, see [../validation-guide.md](../validation-guide.md).
228	
229	---
230	
231	## Phase 4: Response
232	
233	1. **File path** of created/edited workflow
234	2. **Brief description** of what the workflow does
235	3. **Key activities** and logic implemented
236	4. **Packages installed** (if any)
237	5. **Limitations** or notes
238	6. **Suggested next steps** (testing, parameterization)
239	7. **Encourage user to review and customize** (fill placeholders, set up connections)
240	
241	---
242	
243	## Anti-Patterns
244	
245	- **NEVER** generate large, complex workflows in one go
246	- **NEVER** manually craft UI selectors outside of `uia-configure-target` skill flow
247	- **NEVER** assume a create/edit succeeded without validating with **both** `validate` and `build`
248	- **NEVER** treat "no diagnostics found" from `validate` as final — run `build` next; member-name and enum-value errors hide behind a clean `validate`
249	- **NEVER** stop the iteration loop before correctly rendering all activities
250	- **NEVER** guess properties, types, or configurations without checking docs
251	- **NEVER** use incorrect keys with `uip rpa workflow-examples get` (always from list results)
252	- **NEVER** pass absolute paths to `--file-path` in `validate` (must be relative)
253	- **NEVER** ask user to choose provider without checking project signals first
254	- **NEVER** retry failing CLI commands in a loop without diagnosing root cause
255	- **NEVER** skip Phase 0 (Studio readiness)
256	- **NEVER** use connector activities without checking connection existence
257	- **NEVER** ignore activity doc conditional property groups (OverloadGroup conflicts cause validation errors)
258	- **NEVER** generate full XAML from scratch without using `activities get-default-xaml` as a starting point

1	# Common Activity Card
2	
3	**Package anchor:** `UiPath.System.Activities` 26.4 (verified against 26.4.1-preview).
4	
5	Copy-safe snippets for the 13 activities listed below. **Supersedes the Rule 21 discovery procedure for these activities only** — when authoring one of these, skip `activities find`, skip `activities get-default-xaml`, skip the per-activity `<Activity>.md` read, and copy the snippet here.
6	
7	For every other activity, full Rule 21 applies. Self-extending this card by personal judgment ("this one feels simple, I'll skip the procedure") is the failure mode.
8	
9	## Card entries
10	
11	`Sequence` · `If` · `Switch<T>` · `TryCatch` · `While` · `DoWhile` · `ForEach<T>` · `Assign` · `LogMessage` · `WriteLine` · `Delay` · `Throw` · `Rethrow`
12	
13	## How to read the snippets
14	
15	Snippets below are **fragments** intended to drop inside a complete `<Activity>` root. The root must declare:
16	
17	```xml
18	xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities"
19	xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
20	xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"
21	```
22	
23	Entries that need additional prefixes (`xmlns:s` for `System` types, `xmlns:sc` for `System.Collections`) call them out in the "XAML prefix" line. For modern Windows-target projects use `assembly=System.Private.CoreLib`; for Legacy (.NET 4.6.1) projects use `assembly=mscorlib`.
24	
25	Snippets use the property-element form with `<VisualBasicValue>` / `<VisualBasicReference>`. For C# expression projects, apply [xaml/csharp-activity-binding-guide.md](xaml/csharp-activity-binding-guide.md).
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Group A — Control flow
30	
31	### Sequence
32	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.Sequence`
33	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace (`xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/netfx/2009/xaml/activities"`); no `ui:` prefix.
34	
35	**Snippet:**
36	```xml
37	<Sequence DisplayName="Sequence">
38	  <!-- child activities in execution order -->
39	</Sequence>
40	```
41	
42	**Notes:** `Sequence` is the canonical container wrap required by Rule 24 in every body/branch slot of `If`, `Switch`, `TryCatch`, `While`, `DoWhile`, `ForEach`, `Pick`, etc. — even with a single child. Declare `<Sequence.Variables>` only when this sequence owns local variables. ViewState is **optional** for Sequences (Rule 20); required only when the parent is `Flowchart`, `StateMachine`, or `ProcessDiagram`.
43	
44	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Sequence.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Sequence.md)
45	
46	---
47	
48	### If
49	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.If`
50	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; no `ui:` prefix.
51	
52	**Snippet:**
53	```xml
54	<If DisplayName="If">
55	  <If.Condition>
56	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean">
57	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" ExpressionText="counter < 10" />
58	    </InArgument>
59	  </If.Condition>
60	  <If.Then>
61	    <Sequence DisplayName="Then">
62	      <!-- then branch -->
63	    </Sequence>
64	  </If.Then>
65	  <If.Else>
66	    <Sequence DisplayName="Else">
67	      <!-- else branch -->
68	    </Sequence>
69	  </If.Else>
70	</If>
71	```
72	
73	**Notes:** Both `If.Then` and `If.Else` slots must wrap their body in `<Sequence>` per Rule 24. Omit `<If.Else>` entirely when no else branch is needed — do not emit an empty `<If.Else></If.Else>`. For multi-branch `else if … else if`, use `IfElseIfV2` (off this card; see `ElseIf.md`).
74	
75	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/If.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/If.md)
76	
77	---
78	
79	### Switch<T>
80	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.Switch`1`
81	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; no `ui:` prefix.
82	
83	**Snippet** (typed `Int32` example — change `x:TypeArguments` for other types):
84	```xml
85	<Switch x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" DisplayName="Switch">
86	  <Switch.Expression>
87	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
88	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="status" />
89	    </InArgument>
90	  </Switch.Expression>
91	  <Sequence x:Key="1" DisplayName="Case 1">
92	    <!-- case body for status == 1 -->
93	  </Sequence>
94	  <Sequence x:Key="2" DisplayName="Case 2">
95	    <!-- case body for status == 2 -->
96	  </Sequence>
97	  <Switch.Default>
98	    <Sequence DisplayName="Default">
99	      <!-- fallback body -->
100	    </Sequence>
101	  </Switch.Default>
102	</Switch>
103	```
104	
105	**Notes:** Each case body and `Switch.Default` must wrap their content in `<Sequence>` per Rule 24. Case keys are declared via `x:Key="<literal>"` on each case-body child directly inside `<Switch>` — the `Cases` dictionary is not declared explicitly. For string keys: `x:TypeArguments="x:String"` and `x:Key="someString"`.
106	
107	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Switch.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/Switch.md)
108	
109	---
110	
111	### TryCatch
112	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.TryCatch`
113	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; also declare `xmlns:s="clr-namespace:System;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib"` for the exception type (Legacy/.NET 4.6.1 projects use `assembly=mscorlib`).
114	
115	**Snippet:**
116	```xml
117	<TryCatch DisplayName="Try Catch">
118	  <TryCatch.Try>
119	    <Sequence DisplayName="Try">
120	      <!-- guarded body -->
121	    </Sequence>
122	  </TryCatch.Try>
123	  <TryCatch.Catches>
124	    <Catch x:TypeArguments="s:Exception">
125	      <ActivityAction x:TypeArguments="s:Exception">
126	        <ActivityAction.Argument>
127	          <DelegateInArgument x:TypeArguments="s:Exception" Name="exception" />
128	        </ActivityAction.Argument>
129	        <Sequence DisplayName="Catch">
130	          <!-- handler body; reference iterator variable "exception" -->
131	        </Sequence>
132	      </ActivityAction>
133	    </Catch>
134	  </TryCatch.Catches>
135	  <TryCatch.Finally>
136	    <Sequence DisplayName="Finally">
137	      <!-- finally body -->
138	    </Sequence>
139	  </TryCatch.Finally>
140	</TryCatch>
141	```
142	
143	**Notes:** `Try`, every `Catch.Action`, and `Finally` must wrap their body in `<Sequence>` per Rule 24. Each `Catch` requires its own `<ActivityAction x:TypeArguments="...">` holding a `<DelegateInArgument x:TypeArguments="..." Name="exception" />` — the `Name` is the variable name the handler body uses. Place specific exception types before `s:Exception`. Omit `<TryCatch.Finally>` entirely when not needed. For strategy — exception taxonomy, Retry Scope, ContinueOnError, screenshot-on-error, Global Exception Handler — see [error-handling-guide.md](error-handling-guide.md).
144	
145	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/TryCatch.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/TryCatch.md)
146	
147	---
148	
149	### While
150	**Class:** `UiPath.Core.Activities.InterruptibleWhile` (Studio emits **this**, not the framework `System.Activities.Statements.While`)
151	**XAML prefix:** `xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"`.
152	
153	**Snippet:**
154	```xml
155	<ui:InterruptibleWhile DisplayName="While">
156	  <ui:InterruptibleWhile.Condition>
157	    <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" ExpressionText="counter < 10" />
158	  </ui:InterruptibleWhile.Condition>
159	  <ui:InterruptibleWhile.Body>
160	    <Sequence DisplayName="Body">
161	      <!-- iteration body -->
162	    </Sequence>
163	  </ui:InterruptibleWhile.Body>
164	</ui:InterruptibleWhile>
165	```
166	
167	**Non-obvious properties:**
168	- `MaxIterations` — `InArgument<int>` — upper bound; `0` means **unlimited**. Default `0`. Set to a positive value to guard against infinite loops.
169	- `CurrentIndex` — `OutArgument<int>` — zero-based iteration counter; bind to a variable when the body needs the index.
170	
171	**Notes:** Studio uses `InterruptibleWhile`, not the framework `While`. The body must be `<Sequence>`-wrapped per Rule 24. `Condition` is evaluated **before** each iteration; if false on entry, the body never runs.
172	
173	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/While.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/While.md)
174	
175	---
176	
177	### Do While
178	**Class:** `UiPath.Core.Activities.InterruptibleDoWhile` (Studio emits **this**, not the framework `System.Activities.Statements.DoWhile`)
179	**XAML prefix:** `xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"`.
180	
181	**Snippet:**
182	```xml
183	<ui:InterruptibleDoWhile DisplayName="Do While">
184	  <ui:InterruptibleDoWhile.Body>
185	    <Sequence DisplayName="Body">
186	      <!-- iteration body -->
187	    </Sequence>
188	  </ui:InterruptibleDoWhile.Body>
189	  <ui:InterruptibleDoWhile.Condition>
190	    <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" ExpressionText="counter < 10" />
191	  </ui:InterruptibleDoWhile.Condition>
192	</ui:InterruptibleDoWhile>
193	```
194	
195	**Non-obvious properties:**
196	- `MaxIterations` — `InArgument<int>` — upper bound; `0` means **unlimited**. Default `0`.
197	- `CurrentIndex` — `OutArgument<int>` — zero-based iteration counter.
198	
199	**Notes:** Studio uses `InterruptibleDoWhile`, not the framework `DoWhile`. The body must be `<Sequence>`-wrapped per Rule 24. Body executes **at least once**; `Condition` is evaluated **after** each iteration.
200	
201	**Long-form:** [`activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/DoWhile.md`](activity-docs/UiPath.System.Activities/26.4/activities/DoWhile.md)
202	
203	---
204	
205	### For Each<T>
206	**Class:** `UiPath.Core.Activities.ForEach`1` (Studio emits **this**, not the framework `System.Activities.Statements.ForEach<T>`)
207	**XAML prefix:** `xmlns:ui="http://schemas.uipath.com/workflow/activities"`; declare `xmlns:sc="clr-namespace:System.Collections;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib"` for the (non-generic) `IEnumerable` argument typing.
208	
209	**Snippet** (typed `String` example — change `x:TypeArguments` on the outer activity and on the inner `ActivityAction`/`DelegateInArgument` to match the element type):
210	```xml
211	<ui:ForEach x:TypeArguments="x:String" DisplayName="For Each">
212	  <ui:ForEach.Values>
213	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="sc:IEnumerable">
214	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="sc:IEnumerable" ExpressionText="myList" />
215	    </InArgument>
216	  </ui:ForEach.Values>
217	  <ui:ForEach.Body>
218	    <ActivityAction x:TypeArguments="x:String">
219	      <ActivityAction.Argument>
220	        <DelegateInArgument x:TypeArguments="x:String" Name="item" />
221	      </ActivityAction.Argument>
222	      <Sequence DisplayName="Body">
223	        <!-- iteration body; reference iterator variable "item" -->
224	      </Sequence>
225	    </ActivityAction>
226	  </ui:ForEach.Body>
227	</ui:ForEach>

230	**Non-obvious properties:**
231	- `Values` — `InArgument<System.Collections.IEnumerable>` — **non-generic** `IEnumerable`, not `IEnumerable<T>` (verified against `ForEachBase<T>.Values`). The element type `T` comes from the outer `x:TypeArguments` on `<ui:ForEach>`, not from `Values`.
232	- `Body` — `ActivityAction<T>` — must be set via the `<ui:ForEach.Body>` property element (it is NOT the ContentProperty; placing a bare `<ActivityAction>` directly inside `<ui:ForEach>` produces `Cannot set unknown member '...Implementation'`).

234	- `CurrentIndex` — `OutArgument<int>` — zero-based iteration counter.

236	**Notes:** Studio uses `UiPath.Core.Activities.ForEach`, not the framework `ForEach<T>`. The iterator variable name (`item` in the snippet) is set via `DelegateInArgument.Name` on the inner `ActivityAction.Argument` — auto-suggested by Studio based on element type. Body must be `<Sequence>`-wrapped per Rule 24.

242	## Group B — Data + logging
243	
244	### Assign
245	**Class:** `System.Activities.Statements.Assign`1` (generic; preferred) — non-generic `Assign` only when both sides are `object`.
246	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; no `ui:` prefix.
247	
248	**Snippet** (typed `Int32` example):
249	```xml
250	<Assign x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" DisplayName="Assign">
251	  <Assign.To>
252	    <OutArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
253	      <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="counter" />
254	    </OutArgument>
255	  </Assign.To>
256	  <Assign.Value>
257	    <InArgument x:TypeArguments="x:Int32">
258	      <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:Int32" ExpressionText="counter + 1" />
259	    </InArgument>
260	  </Assign.Value>
261	</Assign>

318	**XAML prefix:** standard activities namespace; declare `xmlns:s="clr-namespace:System;assembly=System.Private.CoreLib"` for the `TimeSpan` argument type (Legacy/.NET 4.6.1 projects use `assembly=mscorlib`).

328	</Delay>

    <ui:HttpClient

      EndPoint="["https://wttr.in/Bellevue,WA?format=j1"]"

          <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:Boolean" ExpressionText="isNiceDay" />

                <VisualBasicReference x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="resultMessage" />

                <VisualBasicValue x:TypeArguments="x:String" ExpressionText="$"Not a great day to be outside in Bellevue. Current conditions: {weatherDesc}, {tempF} degrees F. Maybe stay indoors today!"" />

          </Assign>
